Hi Marc —

Great questions. Short answer: both paths can work, but the portal gives better deterministic routing and fewer exceptions for multi-entity bundles. That said, many franchise networks prefer a phased approach (email fallback + portal pilot). I've attached a concise checklist and a sample CSV that our AP ingestion team uses for email-based handoff. High-level notes below.

Portal (recommended for multi-store):
- Accepts multi-invoice PDFs as long as each invoice page includes a store identifier (store number or legal entity UID).
- You can upload a bundle; portal ingestion will attempt to split pages and associate pages to PO numbers if the PO is present on each invoice line.
- For different tax entities we require a store-level entity code in the invoice header.
- Remittance routing can be set per-entity in the vendor profile.

Email (fallback/legacy):
- Use the attached sample_csv_mapping.csv alongside your PDF bundle. CSV should have one row per invoice with columns: filename, store_code, po_number, invoice_date, gross_amount, tax_id, remittance_account.
- Filename convention we prefer: MSF_<storecode>_<YYYYMM>_<INV#>.pdf (this helps automated routing).
- Max single email attachment size: 25MB. For month-end bundles >25MB use SFTP (we provide temporary upload credentials) or split into multiple emails with the CSV mapping referencing all parts.

PO stamping + exceptions:
- If a store cannot provide a PO, you can file as an exception and include a short justification in the CSV 'notes' column; exceptions are reviewed daily but add 3–5 business days.
- To avoid stamping delays, ensure PO numbers are in a consistent column in your CSV and digits only (no dashes).

Next steps:
1) If you want a portal pilot, Vanessa (cc'd) will prepare a vendor profile and invite two pilot stores this week.
2) If you prefer email-first, I included a one-page checklist (franchise_onboarding_form_v2.xlsx) and sample CSV. Please return a completed onboarding form and one sample month bundle so our AP can validate mapping.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to walk through the sample mapping.

Best,

Marc —

Answers inline:
1) Footer store ID: portal OCR will still pick it up but accuracy improves if store_code is in the top 2 lines or consistent footer position. For the pilot, please confirm the exact footer text (copy/paste) and we'll tune the parser rules; we can also add a manual review queue for pages where confidence < 92%.
2) CSV page-range support: yes — the ingestion accepts a 'page_range' column (e.g., "1-4") referencing pages in the bundled PDF. If you use ranges, ensure pages are in the same bundle and the CSV row references the exact filename. Our sample_csv_mapping.csv includes an example row.
3) Webhooks: Jonas (cc'd) runs our payments API. We can enable a per-invoice webhook that posts a small JSON payload with id, status, and reason_code. We'll provide a test endpoint and a shared HMAC secret for verification.

- Next 48 hours: Redwood ingests, runs mapping, and returns a reconciliation CSV and an example webhook event for one invoice.
- Week of 12/13: Expand to 5 pilot stores and validate remittance paths with BrightGate.
